articles.headline: Inside the basketball of 'One Tree Hill' 23 years later
articles.description: In honor of 23 years since "One Tree Hill" premiered, James Lafferty & Co. take us inside the basketball heart of the cult classic TV show.
articles.headlineJa: 23年後の『One Tree Hill』におけるバスケットボールの舞台裏
articles.descriptionJa: 『One Tree Hill』の放送開始から23年を記念し、ジェームズ・ラファティらがこのカルト的人気ドラマの核心であるバスケットボールの裏側を明かす。
articles.body:
WILMINGTON, N.C. -- "Are you here for the big game?" my new friend behind the car rental counter asked shortly after I touched down in Michael Jordan's hometown.

"People are saying you need to be in line by 7 a.m. if you want a chance at a decent seat," she exclaimed before I could answer.

To my surprise, my big game and her big game were one and the same: the "Hey 23" basketball game celebrating 23 years since the hit television show "One Tree Hill" first aired.

Pausing to look around Wilmington International Airport, it appeared nearly everyone arriving in town had the same purpose. Couples, families and groups of friends of all ages -- all donning black, white and royal blue, and not of the Duke Blue Devils variety.

I had counted at least seven combined "Scott" jerseys and two red Quentin Fields-inspired capes before a handmade "You can't kill Dan Scott" sign diverted my attention.

Then the same cheerful voice snapped me back into focus.

"Your car is ready. Just head to spot No. 23! See you tomorrow!"

Unclear whether my rental assignment was intentional or an omen, I grabbed the keys and stepped out into the North Carolina heat.

If a 23rd anniversary feels arbitrary, you're clearly not a "One Tree Hill" fan.

OTH's premise centered around a pair of half-brothers, Lucas (played by Chad Michael Murray) and Nathan Scott (played by James Lafferty) who starred on their high school basketball team in the fictional North Carolina small town of Tree Hill.

The beloved teen drama -- and in my entirely unbiased opinion, the most slept-on basketball show of our generation -- followed Nathan Scott, aka No. 23 and his journey from winning a state championship in high school to being recruited by Duke until his college plans were derailed by his involvement in a point-shaving scheme. Scott eventually went on to win a national title at Maryland before suffering a spinal injury the night before the NBA draft. He then mounted a comeback that started with SlamBall, then saw him play in the D-League and finally become the starting point guard for the then-Charlotte Bobcats.

In the 2000s, Nathan's evolution from a brash high school standout to a selfless NBA star left an indelible mark on a generation of fans. The Ravens never existed -- there was no Tree Hill High and no state championship banner. But for the people who watched the scripted show and the actors who portrayed the characters, the basketball was real. In the years since its historic nine-season run from 2003 to '12, it has amassed a cult following of a magnitude I couldn't quite grasp until setting foot where the show was filmed.

'Hey 23'

On Sept. 19, in front of nearly 5,000 fans at UNC Wilmington's Trask Coliseum, the show's stars, including Lafferty, Murray, Antwon Tanner, Robbie Jones, Bryan Greenberg and Stephen Colletti took the court together again.

articles.headline: Eric Cantona 'wouldn't have joined' Man United if Jim Ratcliffe had been in charge in 90s
articles.description: Manchester United great Eric Cantona has said he would never have joined the club had current co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe been in charge.
articles.body:
Manchester United great Eric Cantona has said he would never have joined the club had current co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe been in charge.

Ratcliffe has courted more controversy this week, saying in a BBC interview that the United Kingdom is in decline because "nobody's tough enough to deal with the immigration problem."

France forward Cantona has previously been named by Ratcliffe as his favourite United player.

But when United fan Pete Boyle, on his TikTok channel, asked Cantona if he would have signed for the club under Ratcliffe, he replied: "No, Of course not.

"You know what I think about all of this, with this kind of politics and I cannot understand that someone like this can say something like this when he's one of the owners of the club.

"Football is a very popular sport. Football is made -- all the greatest players come from different waves of immigration. Everywhere, in France, in England, everywhere.

Cantona moved to Old Trafford in 1992 from rivals Leeds and helped the club win four Premier League titles in five seasons.

articles.headline: Yohandry Morales homers, Nationals bullpen hangs on for a 4-2 win over the Tigers
articles.description: — Yohandy Morales homered for the second time in three games and the Washington Nationals beat the Detroit Tigers 4-2 on Wednesday.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- — Yohandy Morales homered for the second time in three games and the Washington Nationals beat the Detroit Tigers 4-2 on Wednesday.


              Washington has won eight of its last 11 games. Detroit has lost six of eight.


              Will Dion (2-2) picked up the win despite giving up three hits and one run in two innings of relief. Yovanny Cruz got the final four outs for his first save.


              Framber Valdez (10-12) took the loss, allowing two runs in 5 1/3 innings.


              The Nationals ended the scoreless tie with three straight singles to start the sixth. Base hits by Andres Chaparro and Brady House put runners on first and second, and CJ Abrams made it 1-0 with a line drive to right.


              Tyler Kinley relieved Valdez, who gave up a two-run home run to Morales to put the Nationals ahead 3-0. Morales also had a two-run homer on Monday night.


              Detroit's Ben Malgeri led off the bottom of the inning with his fifth home run, a solo shot off Dion, to make it a two-run game.


              Nasim Nunez made it 4-1 in the seventh. He blooped a single to second, stole second and third and scored on a James Wood groundout. The two steals gave him 49 for the season, breaking Abrams' Nationals record of 47, set in 2023. Ron LeFlore has the overall franchise record with 97 in 1980.


              Malgeri made it 4-2 with an RBI single with two out in the ninth, but Cruz retired Riley Greene to end the game.


              Up next
              Nationals: Off Thursday before starting a season-ending three-game series with the New York Mets. LHP Andrew Alvarez (2-6, 3.17) is scheduled to start the opener, while the Mets have not announced their rotation.


              Tigers: Off Thursday before the Pittsburgh Pirates come to Comerica Park to finish the season. RHP Jackson Jobe (2-3, 3,98) will start the opener for Detroit.


              ------

articles.headline: Lamar Jackson, Ravens not focusing on field conditions in Rio
articles.description: A day before the Ravens travel to Brazil to play the Cowboys, quarterback Lamar Jackson said he isn't focusing on the condition of the field at Maracanã Stadium.
articles.headlineJa: ラマー・ジャクソンとレイブンズ、リオのピッチコンディションには囚われず
articles.descriptionJa: レイブンズがカウボーイズとの試合のためにブラジルへ渡る前日、クォーターバック（QB）のラマー・ジャクソンは、マラカナン・スタジアムのグラウンド状態には特に意識を向けていないと語った。
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- A day before the Baltimore Ravens travel to Brazil, quarterback Lamar Jackson said he isn't focusing on the condition of the field at Maracanã Stadium.

"I believe the NFL does a great job at having their specialists go out there and look over the fields," Jackson said Wednesday. "I cannot worry about that. I just have to worry about getting us a dub in Brazil. [As for] the field, we have played on bad fields plenty of times, so I cannot really dwell on that."

On Sunday, Baltimore plays the Dallas Cowboys in the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro.

The concerns about the quality of the playing surface at Rio's Maracanã Stadium started last week when professional soccer players voiced complaints about their home stadium's grass field. On Monday, NFL field director Nick Pappas told ESPN that there are "no concerns right now" about the field conditions in Rio.

Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton has heard about the criticism about the playing surface.

"There is a lot of just, 'he said, she said,' kind of thing going on right now, so we will see," Hamilton said. "I know the players are the product in this league. As soon as we lose 'putting the players forward' is when we lose the league. I am sure the league knows that and they are doing their best to put us in the position to be safe. So, that is not really in the forefront of my mind right now."

Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey said he expects the NFL to have a great field in Rio.

"If we got to play on some concrete, we will play on some concrete," Humphrey said with a smile. "I'm hoping those reports aren't true."

This is the Ravens' first international game since 2023, when they beat the Tennessee Titans 24-16 in London. The Ravens spent the entire week in England to prepare for that game.

For this trip, the Ravens and Cowboys are both flying to Brazil on Thursday night and will arrive Friday, which is two days before the game. The reason Baltimore isn't leaving earlier is because it's only a one-hour time difference.

"I feel like the rhetoric around the game after it is done is who handled the travel and everything better," Hamilton said. "I think that just goes hand in hand on who is being more of a pro or not. That is something that I think we can thrive at. So, I'm excited."

Two Cowboys played in the 2024 game in Sao Paolo and one of their coaches was involved in defensive tackle Kenny Clark, edge rusher Rashan Gary, who were with the Packers, and defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who was with the Eagles.

"It was mushy a little bit," Clark said of the field. "That was in Sao Paulo, so I wonder how the field in Rio is going to look, but yeah, that was a problem last time."

He added, "Of course, I hope it's good, but regardless we're playing on it, so I've got full confidence in the league doing their part and making sure the field is right. And my job is to go out there and put on a great performance."

Pitchers to stream on Thursday

Who had Tyler Mahle as the best deadline acquisition? The veteran lefty is 4-1 with a 1.28 ERA and 0.89 WHIP in eight starts for the Atlanta Braves. Not known for missing bats, Mahle fanned a respectable 44 in those 49 1/3 innings, walking only seven with just four homers allowed. The Braves are locked into the No. 3 seed in the National League, but they'll likely continue to play their regulars until the weekend. This is bad news for the Cincinnati Reds, whose lineup strikes out 25% of the time facing left-handers.

Clay Holmes is slated to start for the Chicago Cubs against the Miami Marlins in the last regular-season game this year at Wrigley Field. The Marlins sport an above-average lineup facing righties, and Holmes has struggled with his control this month, but the Cubs have a lot to play for and the Marlins are just trying to play spoiler. In this scenario, the edge goes to the team with more on the line, and the Cubs are vying for the top National League wild card and home field in the first playoff series.

Peter Lambert has made five straight starts against teams bound for the playoffs or still in contention. His ERA in that span is a solid 3.77, with 27 strikeouts in 28 2/3 innings. The only blemish is a bloated .326 BABIP, and that is out of sync with a stingy 32.6% hard-hit rate over this stretch. The Houston Astros and Texas Rangers are neck-and-neck for the AL West crown, with the loser likely missing the playoffs. Lambert's recent success and a lot to play for gives him the nod against the Athletics, even on the road. Temperatures in Sacramento are more moderate, helping Sutter Health Park play bigger than in the heat of the summer.

Zac Thornton continues to impress for the New York Mets. He'll try to close his season with a third straight quality start when he faces the Rangers in Arlington. The lefty has exhibited pinpoint control with a 5.3% walk rate. The Rangers are a below-average offense facing left-handers.

articles.headline: Vikings RB Aaron Jones working through knee injury
articles.description: The Vikings' offensive backfield is in flux this week as starter Aaron Jones Sr. works through a knee injury and backup Jordan Mason remains on injured reserve.
articles.headlineJa: バイキングスRBアーロン・ジョーンズ、膝の負傷を抱え調整中
articles.descriptionJa: 先発のアーロン・ジョーンズ・シニアが膝の負傷に対応しており、控えのジョーダン・メイソンが故障者リストに入ったままのため、今週のバイキングスのオフェンシブ・バックフィールドは流動的な状態にある。
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings' offensive backfield is in flux this week as starter Aaron Jones Sr. works through a knee injury and backup Jordan Mason remains on injured reserve.

The team planned to hold Jones out of practice Wednesday, coach Kevin O'Connell said, leaving only one running back on its roster who spent time with the team in training camp: rookie Demond Claiborne. Since then, the Vikings have signed three veterans: DeeJay Dallas, Jerome Ford and Jaret Patterson. As of Wednesday, Ford and Patterson were on the practice squad. Dallas was promoted to the 53-man roster last week.

Jones, 31, is coming off one of his best games in years after carrying 23 times for 105 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears. He said afterward that he finished the game while wearing a knee brace. Jones also had a bruise on his left cheek after absorbing a violent hit to the helmet from Bears cornerback Tyrique Stevenson, one that knocked his helmet off.

O'Connell said that Jones feels "pretty good" but gave no indication whether he will be ready to play in the Vikings' game Sunday at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

"We'll just keep getting treatment around the clock," O'Connell said, "and see if we can pick up his workload as the week goes on."

Jones' status is especially notable given the absence of Mason, who fractured his thumb two weeks ago. The Vikings entered the season with Claiborne as their No. 3 back, but he was inactive in Week 1 and got only two snaps in Week 2. Both were pass plays designed for him to get the ball in space. He caught one for 2 yards, and quarterback Carson Wentz scrambled on the other play.

Dallas got two carries and gained 8 yards against the Bears.

articles.headline: In reversal, Chargers not placing Charlie Kolar (forearm) on IR
articles.description: In a surprising reversal, the Chargers are not placing tight end Charlie Kolar on injured reserve after he injured his left forearm in Sunday's game.
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- In a surprising reversal, the Los Angeles Chargers are not placing tight end Charlie Kolar on injured reserve after he injured his left forearm in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.

Coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Kolar would go on injured reserve along with tight end David Njoku, but Kolar's surgery Monday changed his prognosis, and he will remain on the active roster.

Still, Harbaugh said Wednesday that Kolar won't play Sunday against the Buffalo Bills, or practice Wednesday.

With just one healthy tight end on the active roster in Oronde Gadsden, the Chargers signed tight end Hayden Rucci on Tuesday, poaching him from Jacksonville's practice squad.

Rucci is familiar with this Chargers system, having played four games in Miami last season under Mike McDaniel, now offensive coordinator for the Chargers. 

Rucci will likely be ready to contribute as early as Sunday and could be a big help in getting Los Angeles' struggling offense back on track. Gadsden struggles as a run blocker, which puts the offense at a significant disadvantage. Having Rucci, who is already familiar with the system and thrives as a blocker, gives this offense some hope to be multidimensional.
